get.description:
Cursor-paginated list of Midnight markets.

**Use this to discover markets.** For a given user's positions on those markets, follow up with `GET /v0/midnight/users/{user-address}/positions`.

**Filters.** Address filters (`loan_assets`, `collateral_assets`, `oracle_addresses`, `enter_gates`, `liquidator_gates`) must be combined with `chain_ids` — an address alone is not chain-unique. Lowercase addresses are checksummed server-side. Pass `active_only=true` to exclude markets past maturity.

**Pagination.** Response follows the list envelope: `{ cursor, data }`. Pass back `cursor` verbatim on the next call. A `null` `cursor` means the last page.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=5, stale-while-revalidate=2`.

Cursor-paginated feed of Midnight economic transactions for one market.

**Scope.** Includes `borrow`, `lend`, `exit_lend_primary`, `exit_lend_secondary`, `exit_borrow_primary`, `exit_borrow_secondary`, `partial_liquidation`, `full_liquidation`, `withdraw_collateral`, and `supply_collateral`. **Trade actions.** A single trade can affect both the lender and borrower side. Market-level queries can therefore return multiple API items for the same transaction, while account queries return only the items affecting that account. For trade items, `data.assets` is the loan-token amount attributed to the item; `buyer_assets`, `seller_assets`, `take_units`, and `total_units_delta` describe the full trade.

**Filters.** `:market-id` constrains the market and is globally unique across chains. `chain_ids` is optional and can further narrow the query.

**Pagination.** Response follows the list envelope: `{ cursor, data }`. Pass back `cursor` verbatim on the next call. A `null` cursor means the last page. Ordering is fixed to `created_at` with deterministic tie-breakers.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=2, stale-while-revalidate=1`.

get.description:
Cursor-paginated list of a user's active offer groups with nested active offers.

Active offers have started, have not passed their offer expiry or market maturity, and still have remaining group capacity. Asset-capped offers are considered fully consumed when `consumed >= max_assets`; unit-capped offers are fully consumed when `consumed >= max_units`. Fully consumed offers are excluded, and a group is omitted entirely when no active offers remain in it. Each group returns the max `expiry` across all unexpired and unmatured offers in the whole group, including future-start offers, one deterministic representative offer limit (`max_units`, `max_assets`), the latest group-level `consumed` value, and all active offers in that group matching the non-market request filters. Each offer includes both `market_id` and the immutable `market` config used to derive it, because uncreated markets cannot be decoded from `market_id` alone.

**Filters.** `market_ids` filters the group page to groups containing at least one active offer in any requested market, but nested offers are not narrowed by `market_ids`; all active sibling offers in each returned group remain visible. `chain_ids`, `loan_assets`, and `groups` filter both the group page and nested offers. `listed=true` returns only groups where every active offer is on a listed market; `listed=false` returns groups with at least one active offer on an unlisted market. `loan_assets` matches loan token addresses across all chains unless `chain_ids` is also provided. The group-level `expiry` is computed for the whole offer group and is not narrowed by `market_ids` or `loan_assets`. `created_at_gte` and `created_at_lte` filter by the first active matching offer created in each group. `market_ids`, `loan_assets`, and `groups` are capped at 20 values.

**Pagination.** Response follows the list envelope: `{ cursor, data }`. Pagination is over groups; nested offers are not split across pages. Sort groups with `sort_by=id|created_at` and `sort_direction=asc|desc`.

tags.description:
A **Midnight transaction** item is one economic action that changed a market or account. One onchain transaction can appear as multiple API items when it affects more than one side of a trade or more than one account.

### Event types

`borrow`, `lend`, `exit_lend_primary`, `exit_lend_secondary`, `exit_borrow_primary`, `exit_borrow_secondary`, `partial_liquidation`, `full_liquidation`, `withdraw_collateral`, and `supply_collateral`.

Admin, authorization, fee, flashloan, market creation, and accounting-only events are intentionally excluded from v0.

### Amounts

For trade actions, `data.assets` is the loan-token amount attributed to that API item. `buyer_assets`, `seller_assets`, `take_units`, and `total_units_delta` describe the full trade when present.

### User-scoped transactions

`GET /v0/midnight/users/{user-address}/transactions` matches the affected account, not only the transaction caller: buyer/seller for trades, `on_behalf` for primary exits and collateral actions, and borrower for liquidations.

### Market-scoped transactions

`GET /v0/midnight/markets/{market-id}/transactions` returns every economic action for that market, so one onchain transaction can appear as multiple API items when multiple accounts are affected.

### Filters

`chain_ids` is optional on transaction endpoints and can narrow results to supported chains. Currently supported: Base (`8453`). `event_types`, `created_at` ranges, `tx_hash`, `loan_assets`, and `collateral_assets` can further narrow results. User-scoped transactions also accept `market_ids`.

### Sorting

Ordering is fixed to `created_at` with deterministic tie-breakers. Use `sort_direction` to switch between newest-first and oldest-first.
tags.name: Transactions

tags.description:
A **Midnight market** defines a fixed-rate lending venue: one loan token, one maturity timestamp, optional entry/liquidator gates, and a sorted collateral list with LLTV, liquidation cursor, and oracle for each collateral. The `market_id` is stable and unique across supported chains, so it is enough to address a market.

### Filters

Supported chain: Base (`8453`).

Address filters (`loan_assets`, `collateral_assets`, `oracle_addresses`, `enter_gates`, `liquidator_gates`) require `chain_ids` because the same address can exist on multiple chains. Time filters (`maturity_gte`, `maturity_lte`) accept unix seconds; `active_only=true` keeps markets whose maturity is still in the future.

### Sortable fields

`total_units` (default), `maturity`.

tags.description:
A **Midnight position** is a user's current state on a given market: credit, debt, pending fee, loss factor, collateral balances, and — when available — performance analytics.

### Lender vs borrower

A position's `type` is `lend` when `credit > 0`, `borrow` when `debt > 0`, or `collateral_only` when only collateral remains. A position with no credit, no debt, and no remaining collateral is considered **closed** — the detail endpoint returns 200 with zero balances and `type: null` for known markets.

### Cost basis & effective rate

- `cost_basis` uses the **average cost method**: entries add to the basis, exits reduce it proportionally. WAD-scaled bigint in loan-asset units; `null` when the position has no history attributable to the user (e.g. received via transfer).
- `effective_rate_wad` is **IRR+** — the single annualized rate that compounds each remaining buy's capital from entry time to maturity to produce the current face value. WAD-scaled; `null` until sufficient history is available.

The single-position state endpoint omits these two analytics. Use `/position/performance` when you need performance fields.

### Filters

`chain_ids` is required when `loan_assets` is provided. Currently supported: Base (`8453`). Range filters exist on `credit`, `debt`, `cost_basis`, and `effective_rate_wad`.

### Sortable fields

`maturity` (default), `credit`, `debt`, `cost_basis`, `effective_rate_wad`.

tags.description:
Active offer groups for a user.

### Response

List envelope: `{ cursor, data: [...] }`. Pagination is over groups. Filters include `chain_ids`, `market_ids`, `loan_assets`, and `groups`; `chain_ids` currently supports Base (`8453`). `market_ids` selects groups containing at least one active offer in any requested market, but does not hide sibling offers from other markets inside each returned group. `loan_assets` matches loan token addresses across all chains unless `chain_ids` also narrows the query. Active offers have remaining group capacity: asset-capped offers are excluded when `consumed >= max_assets`, and unit-capped offers are excluded when `consumed >= max_units`. A fully consumed group is omitted when no active offers remain in it. Each item contains the group id, chain id, `created_at` from the first active matching offer, `expiry` as the max expiry across unexpired and unmatured offers in the whole group including future-start offers, representative active offer limits, the latest consumed amount for the group, and a nested `offers` array. Nested offers expose the fields needed to display and take an offer; proof metadata and offer hashes are intentionally excluded.
